title: Recursion
misconceptions: A recursive function executes all recursive calls simultaneously in parallel.
A base case is optional if the recursive call terminates on its own.
Recursion can solve computational problems that iteration is theoretically unable to compute.
Recursive calls overwrite the existing local variables of the caller in memory.

rubric.text: Defines recursion as a technique where a function calls itself directly or indirectly.
States that a recursive function requires at least one base case.
Explains that the base case returns a result without making further recursive calls.
States that each recursive call must operate on a strictly smaller subproblem.
Explains that each recursive call pushes an independent stack frame onto the call stack.
States that an absent or unreachable base case triggers a stack overflow error.
Explains that any recursive algorithm can be rewritten iteratively.
Explains that tail call optimization allows compilers to reuse the current stack frame.
